title: OPCON Transition: Now It Is Time for the Commanders-in-Chief
author: Seol In-hyo
text:
U.S. President Donald Trump is escorted by President Lee Jae Myung of South Korea at the Gyeongju National Museum, South Korea, Oct. 29, 2025.
Credit: Official White House Photo by Daniel Torok
The debate over wartime operational control (OPCON) transition once again stands at the threshold of decision. At the 57th Security Consultative Meeting (SCM) in 2025, South Korea and the United States agreed to pursue verification of the full operational capability (FOC) of the Future Combined Forces Command headquarters in 2026, and the 2026 U.S. National Defense Strategy (NDS) assessed that South Korea is capable of taking primary responsibility for deterring North Korea with “critical but more limited” U.S. support. More than 20 years have passed since the allies formalized OPCON transition, and more than a decade of preparation and verification has accumulated since they adopted the conditions-based transition plan. Meanwhile, South Korea has grown into an ally with military and economic capabilities entirely different from those it had when this arrangement was created some 70 years ago.[...]
